You are matching code-review findings against a known bug. Reply with ONLY a JSON object. KNOWN BUG: The dialog's focus trap counts hidden or tabIndex=-1 elements as tabbable (for example the library's own hidden TabPanels inside a Dialog), so Tab moves focus somewhere invisible. Rules: - Answer "yes" only if the text describes THIS specific bug: the same faulty behaviour in the same situation. A finding about a nearby but different behaviour (another header, another edge case, a different race) is "no". - A finding that says the behaviour was checked and PASSED, or that the code handles it correctly, is "no". - Wording does not matter; the behaviour does. - For handoffs: count only text that tells the implementor to fix this bug (a reported finding, a fix instruction). Restated acceptance criteria that merely describe the desired behaviour do NOT count as carrying the finding unless the handoff ties them to a reported failure. === REVIEW 1 FINDINGS === - [blocking] Nested Dialog: Escape closes both dialogs. Both `DialogSurface` instances add a document-level keydown listener (src/Dialog.tsx ~L59-69), so the outer one also fires. Probe P1 opens an inner Dialog from a button inside the outer one, then presses Escape. Output: `P1 inner calls [[false]] outer calls [[false]]`, and the failing assertion is `expected "spy" to not be called at all, but actually been called 1 times`. - [blocking] Nested Dialog: Tab escapes the inner dialog. The outer `keepTabInside` doesn't see the portaled inner dialog's buttons, so it treats focus as outside and pulls it back to the outer button. Probe P2 opens the inner dialog from inside the outer one, then tabs. Output: `P2 after tab open inner` and `expected 'open inner' to be 'innerB'`. README's "Tab and Shift+Tab are kept inside the dialog" is false for nested dialogs. - [minor] Controlled Tabs with a rejected value: arrow keys move DOM focus to the next tab (B) while `selected` stays "a". B keeps `tabIndex=-1`, so the roving tab stop and focus disagree. Probe P3 reported `b.tabIndex` -1 after ArrowRight. Not a criterion violation, but worth a decision. - [minor] `aria-disabled="true"` on a consumer Tab does not disable it. Probe P4 clicked it and ArrowRight'd through it, and `onValueChange` was called with "b" and then "c". T5 accepts either form, and the component's own disabled prop works. Still, the passed-through aria-disabled is ignored. - [minor] Combobox options that change while the listbox is open keep the old index, so the active option silently moves to a different option. Probe P5 showed `aria-activedescendant` pointing at "Zucchini" after the list was swapped, and Enter chose "z". The index is consistent with what's displayed, so this is not a crash. The spec asks for a reset. - [minor] Dialog `description={0}` is silently dropped (P14: `aria-describedby` null, text is only the title). Not reproduced as a spec failure. === REVIEW 2 FINDINGS === - [blocking] Dialog.tsx `openDialogs` ordering is wrong when nested dialogs mount open together. Child passive effects run before parent effects, so the inner layer is pushed first and the outer is last, making the outer the "topmost". Reproduced: `` containing ``, then `{Escape}` gave `outer` calls `[[false]]` and `inner` calls `[]`. Escape-only-topmost is violated for this case. Suggested direction: push in render order or use DOM/tree order, not effect order. - [minor] Dialog backdrop: a mousedown on the backdrop that releases inside the dialog still closes (click target is the common ancestor, the backdrop). Reproduced with `fireEvent.mouseDown(backdrop); fireEvent.mouseUp(dialog); fireEvent.click(backdrop)` → `onOpenChange` called once. The criteria only cover the reverse drag, so this is a judgement call. - [minor] Dialog description `""` (empty string) is "given", so the dialog gets `aria-describedby` pointing to an empty `

`. Not a criterion violation strictly, but the aria-describedby then describes nothing. Reproduced by inspecting the attribute. - [minor] Backdrop close requires a preceding mousedown (`pressedBackdrop` gate). A bare `fireEvent.click(backdrop)` does not close. Real browsers always send mousedown, so this only matters for tests written with fireEvent. === IMPLEMENTOR HANDOFF 1 (sent after review 1) === GOAL: Fix round 1 for the component library in /tmp/ff-eval-5dgunyey/workspace (cwd). You built src/Tabs.tsx, src/Dialog.tsx, src/Combobox.tsx with tests in tests/. A red-team review reproduced the issues below. Fix each one tests-first (add a failing test, then fix), and keep README.md in sync. FILES: src/Dialog.tsx, src/Combobox.tsx, tests/Dialog.test.tsx, tests/Combobox.test.tsx, README.md. FIXES: 1. [blocking] Nested Dialogs, Escape: when an inner Dialog is opened from inside an outer Dialog (both open), Escape currently calls onOpenChange(false) on BOTH, because each DialogSurface adds a document keydown listener. Only the topmost (most recently opened, still open) dialog should handle Escape. Suggested approach: a module-level stack (array) of open dialog refs; push on mount, remove on unmount; the keydown handler returns early unless this dialog is the top of the stack. Test: outer open, open inner from a button inside the outer, press Escape -> inner onOpenChange(false) called, outer's not called. 2. [blocking] Nested Dialogs, Tab trap: with the inner dialog open, Tab moves focus to the outer dialog's button because the outer's trap runs too. Same fix (only topmost handles Tab). Test: Tab and Shift+Tab cycle inside the inner dialog only. 3. Combobox: when `options` changes while the listbox is open, the active index silently points to a different option. Reset the active option (no aria-activedescendant) when the options prop identity changes or the active option is no longer at that index. Simplest: store the active option's *value-independent identity* — e.g. track the active option object itself (`activeOption` state holding the option object) and derive the index via `visible.indexOf(activeOption)`; if not found, there is no active option. Test: open, ArrowDown to an option, rerender with a different options array -> aria-activedescendant absent, Enter does not call onChange. 4. Combobox: `onChange(null)` is part of the API but is never called, so a user can't clear a selection. When the input text is empty and the user blurs or presses Enter (with no active option), and `value !== null`, call `onChange(null)`. Escape still reverts without calling onChange. Tests for blur-clear, Enter-clear, and Escape-after-clearing (no onChange). Document in README props and keyboard tables. 5. Dialog: `description={0}` is dropped because of a truthiness check.
